title: Legislative districts of Misamis Occidental
wikitext:
{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Misamis Occidental''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Misamis Occidental]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts. == History == {{further|Legislative districts of Misamis}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of [[Misamis Occidental]] were represented under the historical [[Misamis (province)|Misamis Province]] (1907–1931). The approval of Act No. 3537 on November 2, 1929, split the old province into [[Misamis Occidental]] and [[Misamis Oriental]], and provided the new provinces separate representations in the [[Philippine Assembly]].{{cite journal|author=Philippine Legislature|title=Public Laws enacted by the Philippine Legislature during the period August 9, 1929 to February 7, 1930 comprising Acts Nos. 3529 to 3672|journal=Public Resolutions, Etc |series=Laws, etc |date=1930|publisher=Bureau of Printing|url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.35112102880772;view=1up;seq=119|access-date=November 18, 2017|format=Digitized and uploaded by University of Michigan on March 9, 2016}} The new province of Misamis Occidental first elected its [[#Lone District (defunct)|own representative]] in the [[1931 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1931 elections]]. It also remained part of the [[Senatorial districts of the Philippines#Eleventh District|eleventh senatorial district]] which elected two out of the 24-member [[Senate of the Philippines|upper house]] of the [[Philippine Legislature]] when senators were still elected from territory-based districts (1916–1935). During the [[Second World War]], the Province of Misamis Occidental sent [[#At-Large (defunct)|two delegates]] to the [[National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic|National Assembly]] of the Japanese-sponsored [[Second Philippine Republic]]: one was an [[ex officio member|''ex officio'' member]], while the other was elected through a provincial assembly of [[KALIBAPI]] members during the [[Japanese occupation of the Philippines]]. Upon the restoration of the [[Philippine Commonwealth]] in 1945 the province retained its pre-war [[#Lone District (defunct)|lone district]]. Even after receiving their own city charters, [[Ozamiz]], [[Tangub]] and [[Oroquieta]] remained part of the representation of the Province of Misamis Occidental by virtue of Section 89 of Republic Act No. 321 (June 19, 1948),{{cite web|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/4_republicacts.php?id=320|date=June 19, 1948|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=November 19, 2017|title=Republic Act No. 321 – An Act Creating the City of Ozamiz}} Section 88 of Republic Act No. 5131 (June 17, 1967),{{cite web|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/52_republicacts.php?id=5135|date=June 17, 1967|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=November 19, 2017|title=Republic Act No. 5131 – An Act Creating the City of Tangub}} and Section 106 of Republic Act No. 5518 (June 21, 1969),{{cite web|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/56_republicacts.php?id=5522|date=June 21, 1969|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=November 19, 2017|title=Republic Act No. 5518 – An Act Creating the City of Oroquieta}} respectively. Misamis Occidental was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region X]] from 1978 to 1984. The province returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|one representative, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province was reapportioned into two congressional districts;{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 19, 2017}} each elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. == [[Misamis Occidental's 1st congressional district|1st District]] == *'''[[Cities of the Philippines|City]]''': [[Oroquieta]] *'''[[Municipalities of the Philippines|Municipalities]]''': [[Aloran]], [[Baliangao]], [[Calamba, Misamis Occidental|Calamba]], [[Concepcion, Misamis Occidental|Concepcion]], [[Jimenez, Misamis Occidental|Jimenez]], [[Lopez Jaena]], [[Panaon, Misamis Occidental|Panaon]], [[Plaridel, Misamis Occidental|Plaridel]], [[Sapang Dalaga]] *'''Population (2024)''': 276,944{{cite web |date=July 17, 2025 |title= 2024 Census of Population (POPCEN) Population Counts Declared Official by the President |url=https://psa.gov.ph/content/2024-census-population-popcen-population-counts-declared-official-president |access-date=July 18, 2025 |work=Philippine Statistics Authority}} {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; width:40%;" |- ! width="40%"| Period !
